value.body: Helps businesses register under GST, file returns, reconcile input tax credit and respond to notices, acting on their behalf as an enrolled GST practitioner. Practitioners work independently, in CA or tax-consultant firms, or in company tax teams. Work peaks around monthly and quarterly return due dates.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Com, BBA, a law degree, or a CA/CMA/CS course

items.label: Enrolment
items.value: Form GST PCT-01 on the GST portal
items.note: Under Rule 83 of the CGST Rules

items.label: Exam
items.value: GST practitioner exam conducted by NACIN
items.note: Must be passed within the period allowed after enrolment

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Eligible routes include a graduate or postgraduate degree in commerce, law, banking (including higher auditing), business administration or business management, among others listed in the rules. The steps are to enrol on the GST portal and then pass the NACIN exam. Most freshers first work in a tax consultant's or CA firm to learn filings on real client files.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: GST registration and return filing (GSTR-1, GSTR-3B)

value.title: At a glance
items: Rules and forms change often; tracking notifications is a constant part of the work.
Many practitioners build an independent client base over time.
Next steps: tax associate → tax manager, or an independent practice; some go on to CA or CMA.
